plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle kidney samples, unpaired, single batch). The design is a simple two-group comparison, so a standard DESeq2 workflow is appropriate: build the DESeqDataSet from the raw integer count matrix and the condition column in metadata, run the Wald test for treated vs control, and extract the full DE gene table with shrunken log2FC, p-values and FDR. That gene-level statistic (signed t-statistic or shrunken LFC/stat) is then the direct input to TF activity inference: decoupleR's univariate linear model (ulm) or weighted mean method run against the DoRothEA human regulon (confidence A-C, available in the reference store for Homo sapiens) infers which transcription factors' target programs are coordinately shifted between aldosterone and vehicle. A pathway enrichment step on the same DE signature, using WikiPathways human gene sets, gives orthogonal functional context (e.g. mineralocorticoid/steroid signaling, ion transport) to help interpret which TFs are biologically plausible drivers versus statistical artifacts of a small n=6 per arm design. All steps operate on the actual counts.csv/metadata.csv files with the actual 6-vs-6 aldosterone/vehicle contrast — no other comparison is available in this dataset.
